biography:
Cláudio Ricci's journey to the Ligier JS P320 cockpit began amidst the vibrant chaos of São Paulo's karting scene. His father, a mechanic with a passion for Formula One, introduced him to the sport at a young age. Ricci's raw talent was evident from the start, but it was his relentless defensive driving style that truly set him apart. He quickly climbed the ranks, earning a reputation for making his car incredibly wide, much to the frustration of his competitors. Despite early successes in Formula 3 Brazil, Ricci faced sponsorship challenges that threatened to derail his career. A breakthrough came during a one-off race in the European Le Mans Series, where his gritty performance caught the eye of a Ligier team manager. 

Ricci's career has been a testament to perseverance. He often recalls a pivotal moment during his early karting days when his kart broke down in the middle of a race. Instead of giving up, he pushed the kart across the finish line, earning the respect of his fellow racers. This never-give-up attitude has become his trademark. While he may not always have the outright pace of some of his rivals, his tactical brilliance and unwavering focus make him a formidable opponent. 

Currently, Ricci is considered to be at the peak of his career. He has secured a multi-year contract with Ligier and is determined to compete for championship titles. He is known for his meticulous preparation and unwavering commitment to his team. He is also a vocal advocate for driver safety and is actively involved in promoting motorsport in Brazil.

His ultimate goal is to compete at the 24 Hours of Le Mans and to bring home a victory for Brazil.
drivingStyle: Ricci's driving style is characterized by his exceptional defensive skills and tactical acumen. He is a master of blocking maneuvers and is renowned for his ability to position his car perfectly to prevent overtaking. While he may not always be the fastest driver on the track, he is incredibly consistent and rarely makes mistakes. He excels in managing tire wear and fuel consumption, often gaining an advantage in the later stages of a race. Ricci's approach is calculated and methodical, prioritizing consistency and reliability over outright speed. He is a true strategist on the track, always thinking several steps ahead of his competitors.

rivalries.name: Jean-Pierre Dubois
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial collision during a Formula 3 race that cost Ricci the championship.

rivalries.name: Alessia Russo
rivalries.reason: Russo, known for her aggressive overtaking, constantly challenges Ricci's defensive driving style, leading to numerous on-track battles.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: Tanaka accused Ricci of unfair blocking tactics after a particularly frustrating race in the Asian Le Mans Series.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of racing socks, even if they're falling apart.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba song before every race to calm his nerves.
Refuses to eat anything with pineapple on race weekends.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't always about being the fastest; it's about being the smartest and the most persistent."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2022 European Le Mans Series race at Monza after starting from the back of the grid due to a mechanical failure in qualifying. He strategically conserved fuel and tires to pull off a remarkable victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the 2021 24 Hours of Daytona while leading his class with only two hours remaining. A mechanical failure caused him to lose control, ending his team's hopes of victory.
